# Independent audit of arbitrary-direction simplex chords

Audited source: `candidate 588e75e8ff86db2e`.

**Result: substantive mathematical proof PASS.** One literal dimension
wording correction is required: the image of x -> (a_i.x) is the
d-dimensional coordinate hyperplane in R^(d+1), not an m-dimensional
hyperplane when m=d+1. This does not affect any displayed formula.

## Measure and overlap

Because a_0.e=1, the determinant of the coordinates x=y+t e, with
y in ker(a_0) measured by orthonormal (d-1)-volume, is1/||a_0||.
This verifies the exact transverse measure, even for an oblique e.

The inequalities for T intersect (T-s e) correctly use the positive
parts of a_i.e. Their total slack is m-s sigma. Splitting their
right sides into a common value rho and a coordinate vector of sum0
gives a unique translation, because the normal map has rank d and
image exactly that hyperplane. At rho=0, all the translated inequalities
force equality and therefore one point; for rho<0 their sum is
inconsistent. The overlap volume and maximum chord length L=m/sigma
follow exactly.

On each line the overlap has length(ell-s)_+. Difference quotients
are bounded by1 on a finite transverse projection, so differentiation
under the integral is justified. Right and left derivatives give the
stated positive-level tail and absence of atoms. For d>=2 its limit
at L is0, excluding a top atom. The transverse projection is a
full-dimensional convex body in ker(a_0); its boundary is null, and
every interior projected line has a positive-length section. Thus
nu{ell>0}=nu(pi_e T)=P, as used by the source.

## Rearrangement and all constants

The signed threshold comparison is valid both for indicator supports
and fractional selectors. The chord distribution has no positive atom,
so there is no unresolved partial-level choice. Direct integration gives

    integral_(L(1-eta))^L v [P(d-1)/L](1-v/L)^(d-2)dv
      =V[d eta^(d-1)-(d-1)eta^d].

Its strict derivative on0<eta<1 and endpoint values establish the
unique quantile parameter. The support lower bound follows by monotone
threshold comparison, without presuming a minimizing subbody exists.
The b=V case correctly uses equality of the section integrals; it may
also be justified by equal-volume convex containment B=T.

The roof inequality retains the positive quantity H-m and sigma>=1
in the correct directions. Both versions of equation(9) dominate Hb/m;
for the direction-free version one can check directly that

    (Vd/m)eta^(d-1) >= b/m

from its defining volume formula.

For the final swept-segment application, no coordinate translation is
needed: the actual segment has a fixed transverse coordinate y_A, and
the section of S+B at y_A+y is[l+L_B(y),h+U_B(y)]. Transverse translation
invariance then yields exactly R_e. The endpoints straddle0 because
l<-1, U_B<=1, h>d, and L_B>=-d. Midpoint scaling is2^d exactly.

The theorem is correctly limited to a geometric input. It constructs
no mixed-integer center, and neither a sharp all-dimensional roof
constant nor an OC conclusion is inferred.

## Actual convex sharpness of the projection-volume bound

The standalone projection bound is sharp even among actual convex
subbodies, in every allowed direction e. The chord function ell(y) is
concave on the transverse projection: interpolating two interval
sections places their interval interpolation in the intermediate section,
whose length is consequently at least the interpolated lengths.
Therefore E={y:ell(y)>=v_0} is convex. For the quantile v_0 in(7), set

    B=T intersect pi_e^(-1)(E).

This is convex and compact; for0<b<V, the chord distribution gives E
positive transverse measure and hence interior, with v_0<L. Thus B
has nonempty d-dimensional interior. Its entire section over each y
in E is the T section, so its volume is exactly b and its projection
measure is exactly P eta^(d-1). At b=V take B=T. This proves sharp
attainment of the projection-volume inequality; it makes no claim
that the later roof lower estimate is sharp.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
